goal: Replace the OS-driven prefers-color-scheme theming in packages/ui/src/tokens/theme.css with an explicit user-controlled theme preference, defaulting to light, chosen from a settings screen rather than inherited automatically from the OS/browser.
outcome: The extension renders in light mode by default regardless of OS theme. A user can flip a Light/Dark toggle added directly as an item in the main-screen's existing gear menu (the same inline menu that already lists "Lock & auto-lock" and "Network & peers" -- no new screen or route); the choice is persisted and applied consistently across popup, sidepanel, and approval entrypoints on next render. theme.css's dark-mode token block is switched from a `prefers-color-scheme` media query to a class/attribute-based selector driven by the stored preference, with every existing token name unchanged so no consumer needs to change.

requirements.statement: Do not add a 'system/auto' option — this intent's scope is exactly two states, light and dark, chosen by the user; light is the default for a wallet with no stored preference yet.

packages/ui/src/tokens/theme.css keeps every existing --color-* token name unchanged; only the selector gating the dark-mode @theme block changes, from `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` to a class/attribute selector (e.g. `[data-theme="dark"]`) so no consuming component needs to change.

The stored preference must be readable before first paint in each entrypoint (popup, sidepanel, approval) to avoid a light-to-dark flash; follow the existing storage adapter pattern (apps/extension/src/adapters/storage.ts) rather than introducing a second storage mechanism.

No new screen, route, or file under a settings-home-shaped path is introduced -- the toggle is one more item in the existing inline gear menu (apps/extension/entrypoints/popup/main-screen/src/MainScreenView.tsx's settings menu, alongside "Lock & auto-lock" and "Network & peers"), consistent with settings-screens-gap's documented reason that menu is inline rather than a dedicated settings-home screen.
A fresh install with no stored preference and an OS set to dark mode still renders light.
Flipping the toggle in the gear menu persists across popup close/reopen and is reflected in the sidepanel and approval windows.
